source_text: Sacerdos mundum pronuntiat cum sanitas redit. Christus absolvit. Noli redire ad vomitum. Amen.
thought_title: The priest declares clean when healing returns
orientation: Origen is concluding his homily on the cleansing of leprosy, applying the priest's declaration of cleanness to Christ's absolution and warning against returning to sin.
pass_a_gloss: The priest declares clean when health returns. Christ absolves. Do not return to vomit. Amen.

choices.why: The priest's official declaration of ritual cleanness, matching the Levitical context of the homily.
Christ's action is judicial and personal, releasing the sinner from guilt, not merely declaring a state.
The phrase echoes Proverbs 26:11 and 2 Peter 2:22, warning against returning to sin after cleansing; kept literal to preserve the vivid image.
rejected: Do not go back to your vomit

choices.why: The healing is described as a return of health, not a new creation, fitting the Levitical inspection process.

pass_b_english: The priest declares it clean when health returns. Christ absolves. Do not return to vomit (Proverbs 26:11; 2 Peter 2:22). Amen.
